BACKGROUND. This is a two-person video podcast pipeline. Episode episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho ("Fred Cho", E104) has finished media: final/episode.mp3 and final/episode.mp4 both exist and pass preflight, and its audio was independently certified on the session grid at 0.0ms drift across 12 probe points. What blocks publication is PACKAGING, not media.

The episode's publish preflight currently reports 3 pass, 7 fail, 1 skip. Run it yourself to see the live state:

  cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from server.pipeline.publish_preflight import evaluate_episode;r=evaluate_episode('episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho');[print('%-22s %s %s' % (c['name'],c['status'],c.get('detail',''))) for c in r['checks']]"

Read server/pipeline/publish_preflight.py to see exactly what each check requires. Do not guess at the requirements; the file is the contract.

IMPORTANT: machinery for this already exists. You are running and wiring existing generators, not inventing a packaging system. Find and use what is there before writing anything new.

YOUR LANE: produce the three missing artwork assets for this episode.

server/pipeline/thumbnail.py already contains generate_thumbnail, generate_podcast_artwork and generate_episode_artwork. Read their signatures and use them. Do not write a new renderer.

The preflight requires exactly these three files to exist:
  episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/final/thumbnail.png
  episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/final/podcast-artwork.png
  episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/social-image.png

Write a small, reusable, idempotent script at scripts/generate_episode_assets.py that takes an episode directory and generates all three using the existing generators, then RUN it for this episode so the files exist. Reusable means the next episode can run the same script; do not hard-code this episode anywhere in it.

Pull the guest name and title from the episode's own episode.json rather than inventing them. If a required input such as a headshot is missing, the existing generators already have fallbacks; use them rather than adding new assets.

Do not invent brand colours, fonts or layout: thumbnail.py already defines them.

You own exactly one file: scripts/generate_episode_assets.py. You may also create the three image outputs, which are episode artifacts rather than source. Do not edit any other source file.

HOW THIS RUNS, read carefully because it changes what you produce. The episode directory is GITIGNORED and its media is not in git, and you do not have write access to the live repository. So you do NOT run anything against the real episode. Your deliverable is the SCRIPT ITSELF, written into your own working directory, and the coordinator executes it against the live estate afterwards.

Read /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast freely; it is readable. Write only your one script, at the filename given below, in your current working directory.

Because you cannot test against the real episode, be defensive: validate inputs, fail loudly with a useful message when a required file is missing, and never write partial output. A script that half-succeeds on someone else's estate is worse than one that refuses.

YOUR ONE DELIVERABLE: ./generate_episode_assets.py in your current working directory.
